title: Energy Efficient Convolutions with Temporal Arithmetic
problem: Convolution operations dominate power consumption through multiply-accumulate operations, and while analog-to-time converters use less energy than ADCs, arithmetic manipulation of temporally encoded signals has been limited to simple operations like min, max, and delay, making convolution on temporal signals impossible.
motivation: Reducing power consumption in convolution operations is critical for sensor-integrated computing and neural networks where MAC operations and data movement are the primary energy consumers.
method: The paper develops techniques to perform arithmetic operations directly on temporally encoded analog signals without requiring complete ADC conversion. They implement multiply-accumulate operations on time-domain encoded data, leveraging temporal arithmetic primitives to enable efficient convolution computation while preserving the energy advantages of analog-to-time conversion.
key_novelty: Demonstrating that practical arithmetic manipulation and convolution operations are possible directly on temporally encoded signals, not just simple temporal operations.
contributions: First arithmetic convolution directly on temporally encoded signals without ADC conversion
Practical circuit implementation of temporal multiply-accumulate operations
Energy-efficient convolution mechanism for sensor-fused computation
Demonstration that temporal arithmetic is feasible for complex operations beyond min/max/delay
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; scalability to larger networks and practical silicon results not detailed.
